bridges.description: Defend the rationality of theistic belief and add a positive comparative argument that God better explains human access to objective moral facts.
Establish that belief in God can arise rationally and non-inferentially under suitable experiential conditions.
Defend transcendent personal agency as a legitimate kind of philosophical explanation rather than a placeholder by definition.
Infer that a perfectly good personal creator better explains human access to objective moral facts.
Block evidential arguments from hiddenness, cosmic hostility, and apparently pointless suffering by challenging their theistic likelihood assumptions.
Infer that naturalism is preferable to classical theism and therefore that the God defined for the debate does not exist.
Give naturalism a pre-evidential advantage because classical theism makes additional specific claims.
Compare how expected the observed evidence is under naturalism and classical theism.
Use nonresistant unbelief and the value of conscious reciprocal relationship as evidence favoring naturalism.
Use cosmic hostility together with scale and apparently pointless suffering as evidence favoring naturalism.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Naturalistic reduction and Platonist realism leave human truth-directed moral cognition unexplained, while God supplies a personal explanation of that capacity.
moves.warrant: Rauser argues that reductionism sacrifices objective moral information and that Platonism leaves unexplained how intuition accesses inert abstract goodness; an omnipotent, morally perfect creator has both motive and ability to equip rational agents to grasp moral facts.

moves.importanceRationale: Rauser identifies this as his positive test case for belief based on a feature of the world.

burdenContact.rationale: It supplies the positive evidential inference from moral knowledge to God.
